justification.text: `(p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1)` is the problem's quotient (p^q - 1)/(p - 1); the denominator is nonzero because p is prime so p ≥ 2, and the natural-number division is exact because p - 1 divides p^q - 1 (the quotient is the geometric sum 1 + p + … + p^{q-1}), so Lean's `/` returns the integer the problem means.

`(q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1)` is the problem's quotient (q^p - 1)/(q - 1); the denominator is nonzero because q is prime so q ≥ 2, and the natural-number division is exact because q - 1 divides q^p - 1 (the quotient is 1 + q + … + q^{p-1}), so Lean's `/` returns the integer the problem means.
`p - 1` never truncates because p is prime (hypothesis `hp`), so p ≥ 2 and p - 1 ≥ 1 as an integer.
`p ^ q - 1` never truncates because p is prime, so p ≥ 2 and p^q ≥ 2 > 1, hence p^q - 1 ≥ 1 as an integer.
`q - 1` never truncates because q is prime (hypothesis `hq`), so q ≥ 2 and q - 1 ≥ 1 as an integer.
`q ^ p - 1` never truncates because q is prime, so q ≥ 2 and q^p ≥ 2 > 1, hence q^p - 1 ≥ 1 as an integer.
